title: The Letter of Vilna
premise: In 1912, Elodie Thornbury is summoned to the Vilna Observatory to repair its failing master clock, only to discover a hidden letter implicating her adoptive father in a decades-old betrayal that destroyed another family. When the season's first snows close the bridge and trap the observatory's residents together, old loyalties fracture: her father's patron demands silence, her brother wants the truth sold, and the wronged family's last surviving daughter arrives seeking answers. As the clock's mechanism becomes both evidence and metaphor, Elodie must decide whether protecting the found family that raised her matters more than the truth — and when the thaw finally opens the bridge, she chooses truth, sending the letter forward while keeping the family that chose her, at the cost of the father who didn't.
about_author: Edmund Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing correspondence in Eastern European municipal records before turning to fiction. He writes historical novels about the small betrayals that history forgets but families never do.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Summoned from her workshop to the Vilna Observatory, she repairs the master clock while navigating the careful silences of her adoptive father Aurel, the head horologist. She notices his fear when the observatory's patron, Count Brasov, visits unannounced. Emotional beat: unease — fifteen years of learned silence beginning to chafe.

chapters.title: What the Case Conceals
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Deep inside the clock's housing she finds a sealed letter dated 1897, addressed to a family named Vaitkus, bearing Aurel's handwriting. She hides it, telling no one. Emotional beat: dread — the first crack in the foundation of her found family.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Aurel. Early snow seals the gorge bridge; the observatory is cut off until spring. Aurel realizes the letter is missing; Elodie realizes he knows. A tense dinner where everyone performs normalcy. Emotional beat: claustrophobia — the trap closes on everyone at once.

chapters.title: A Guest at the Gate
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Through the storm comes Magda Vaitkus, the daughter of the betrayed family, stranded and taken in. She carries her own copy of an old grievance and doesn't know Aurel's face. Elodie, hosting her, feels loyalty split down the middle. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Count Brasov's Kindness
chapters.summary: Aurel's POV. Flashbacks interwoven with present: how Brasov saved Aurel from ruin in 1897 and demanded complicity in forging documents that stripped the Vaitkus estate. Now Brasov, also snowbound, quietly reminds Aurel what silence has bought them all. Emotional beat: corruption revealed as gratitude weaponized.

chapters.title: Brother Against Winter
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV (Elodie's brother). Tomas discovers the letter and sees not betrayal but leverage — Brasov will pay handsomely for it. He tries to recruit Elodie, framing it as securing their future. Their argument tears at the found family's seams. Emotional beat: temptation — loyalty priced in coin.

chapters.title: Magda's Story
chapters.summary: Magda's POV. She tells Elodie about her family's destruction — the forged debts, her father's suicide, her mother's exile — never knowing the man across the dinner table caused it. Elodie nearly confesses twice and fails. Emotional beat: shame curdling into the necessity of truth.

chapters.title: The Clock Stops
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The master clock fails catastrophically; Aurel, repairing it beside her, admits everything — the letter was meant to be sent, Brasov intercepted it, and cowardice did the rest. He begs her to let the past stay buried for the family's sake. Emotional beat: confession as both relief and ultimatum.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. A supply sled arrives before the final freeze — room for only one person to leave. Brasov maneuvers to send Tomas away with the letter bought and destroyed; Aurel offers the berth to Elodie to escape the whole affair. Instead Elodie gives the berth to Magda, sends the letter with her, and confronts Brasov before the assembled household. Emotional beat: climax — truth chosen over safety, at real cost.

chapters.title: What Keeps Time
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, spring. The bridge reopens; investigators come; Aurel accepts consequence with unexpected grace, and Brasov's patronage collapses. Tomas leaves in anger; Magda returns in forgiveness. Elodie repairs the clock one final time and winds it herself. Emotional beat: resolution — found family remade on honest terms, time kept truthfully.
